outputs.exact_statement: For every $(\Omega,a,b,m)$ as above, there is a curve law $\mu_{\Omega,a,b,m}$ such that, for every sequence with mesh tending to zero and satisfying all the preceding domain, marked Carathéodory, angle and nome assumptions, $$\mathcal L(\chi_\delta\circ\gamma_\delta) \ \Longrightarrow\ \chi_*\mu_{\Omega,a,b,m}$$ in the metric [mod:curve-metric], along the full sequence. The physical prime-end curve law $\mu_{\Omega,a,b,m}$ is independent of the lattices, admissible domain approximations and nome sequence.* *For $m>0$, $\mu_{\Omega,a,b,m}$ is the unique law in Definition 3. For $m<0$, it is the reversal of the positive-mass law in $(\Omega,b,a)$ with mass $|m|$, with primal and dual boundary labels interchanged. In either case we call it thermal massive $\mathrm{SLE}_{16/3}$.

Equation [mod:bvp] has exactly one solution in this class. It satisfies $0\le h\le1$. On interior compact sets, $h$ and its first derivatives depend continuously on the marked domain in the Carathéodory topology, when the domains lie in a fixed bounded physical region.

Consider the weights of Section [mod:section], with $r_\delta/\delta\to m/2$, on isoradial meshes whose rhombus half-angles belong to $[\eta,\pi/2-\eta]$.* 1. *For marked Carathéodory convergence to a bounded simply connected two-point domain, the reconstructed two-point FK fermion converges locally uniformly, up to its common sign, to a smooth massive-holomorphic function $f$: $$\bar\partial f+\mathrm im\overline f=0.$$ Its square integral $h$, normalized by its two boundary values, is the unique bounded solution $$\Delta h=-4m|\nabla h|,\qquad h=1\ \hbox{on the wired bank},\qquad h=0\ \hbox{on the dual-wired bank}.$$ The boundary values are prime-end limits away from the two marked ends, and $0\le h\le1$. The convergence includes uniform interior bounds on protected compact subsets.* 2. *For every fixed rectangle aspect ratio and every finite physical scale bound, the crossing probabilities of both colors are bounded away from zero, uniformly over all boundary conditions and all nondegenerate lattice rectangles below that scale whose side lengths exceed a fixed multiple of the mesh. The scale constants are independent of the mesh.

After any finite sequence of these revelations, the unqueried continuing problem is an isoradial Dobrushin problem with the same interior weights. Its two banks are the old banks extended by the revealed diagonals. All discrepancies between the geometric slit and this graph domain occur in a bounded number of cell layers along the slit, together with components cut off from the continuation. The conditional probabilities of the two outcomes of a genuine new pairing are uniformly bounded below.

Let $A=A(z;r,R)$ be a physical annulus with $R\le L_1$, where $L_1$ is fixed. Inside $A$, let $\mathcal V$ be a union of regions whose accessible noncircular banks all have one color, and let $c$ be the other color. Circular ends may carry arbitrary induced boundary identifications. After buffering the two ends by a fixed number of cell layers, the probability of an actual $c$-arm crossing $A$ in any of the regions is at most $$K\left(\frac{r\vee\delta}{R}\right)^\alpha.
 \label{geo:arm-bound}$$ The constants are independent of the number of regions and remain valid after arbitrary conditioning outside buffered shells. For specified disjoint buffered annuli the corresponding upper bounds can be multiplied.
The regularly drawn medial interfaces in domains of diameter at most $L$ satisfy condition G2 of [[KS](#ref-KS)], uniformly over the allowed meshes, domains, and thermal parameters.

Let $V_n$ be simply connected planar domains containing $z_0$, and let $\chi_n:V_n\to\mathbb D$ satisfy $\chi_n(z_0)=0$ and the same angular normalization. Suppose $$0<c_0\le \operatorname{crad}_{V_n}(z_0)\le C_0<\infty.$$ If $E_n\subset V_n$ is connected and $\operatorname{diam}E_n\to0$, then $\operatorname{diam}\chi_n(E_n)\to0$. The same conclusion holds after adjoining accessible prime-end endpoints approached along $E_n$. In particular, bounded-cell changes of a mesh tending to zero have vanishing diameter in the normalized disc, provided their incident sectors are respected.

Under the common diameter bound, the laws of the interfaces transferred by their normalized maps to the closed disc are tight in the oriented curve metric. Every subsequential limit is a chordal Loewner trace with a continuous driving function and strict capacity growth. It reaches the target only at the end and is continuously completed in disc coordinates. Along a further coupling, the curves and their half-plane drivers converge jointly, with uniform convergence of the drivers and capacity-parametrized curves on every finite capacity interval.

In a coupling as in Proposition 11, let $t_n\to t<\infty$. The active graph domains at the corresponding exploration times converge in the marked Carathéodory sense to $O_t$, locally from any protected point in $O_t$. Their moving corner converges to the prime end represented by $W_t$. The assertion includes contacts of the limiting trace with itself or with an original bank.

Every subsequential curve law of Proposition 11 has a joint realization with a complex field $M_t(w)$, $w\in O_t$, such that $$M_t(w)^2=D h_t(w),\qquad \bar\partial M_t+\mathrm im\overline{M_t}=0.$$ The field is continuous locally in space and time before swallowing, and is smooth in its spatial variable. On every protected compact subset of the live domain, after localization, $M_t(w)$ is a continuous martingale in the joint natural filtration of the curve and field. In particular it is a continuous local martingale at each fixed point before its swallowing time.

Before the point’s lifetime, $$\label{eng:clock-identities}
 Y_s=Y_0e^{-2s},\qquad
 \mathrm d\log\operatorname{crad}_{O_{t(s)}}(w)=-4X_s^2\,\mathrm ds,
 \qquad \mathrm dt=r_s^2\,\mathrm ds.$$ The same identities hold after any live stopping time, with elapsed capacity and clock times and the corresponding starting values.

There exist $p\in(0,1/4)$, $b>0$, and $K<\infty$ such that, from every live restart, $$\label{eng:moment-decay}
 \mathbb E[X_s^p\mid\text{past}]\le K X_0^p e^{-bs},\qquad s\ge0.$$ The same choice of $p$ has a uniformly bounded conditional $2p$-moment of $\sup_{s\ge0}X_s/X_0$.

The subsequential driving process is a continuous semimartingale and, in the above joint filtration, satisfies $$\mathrm dW_t=\sqrt{\frac{16}{3}}\,\mathrm dB_t+
                \frac{2\pi}{3}C_t\,\mathrm dt,
 \qquad
 \int_0^T C_t^2\,\mathrm dt<\infty\quad\text{almost surely for every }T<\infty,
 \label{cal:driver-equation}$$ where $B$ is a Brownian motion and $$C_t=\frac4\pi\int_{\mathbb H}P(v)\mu_t(v)
              |\nabla(h_t\circ\psi_t)(v)|\,\mathrm dA(v).
 \label{cal:C-definition}$$ In particular, neither absolute continuity of the quadratic variation nor absolute continuity of the finite-variation part of $W$ is an assumption of the argument.

There is a constant $K$, depending only on $m$ and a physical diameter bound, such that on every active domain $$\begin{aligned}
 h_t(z)&=u_t(z)+4m\int_{O_t}G_t(z,w)|M_t(w)|^2\,\mathrm dA(w),
 \label{cal:representation}\\
 |M_t(w)|^2&\leq \frac{K}{\operatorname{crad}_{O_t}(w)}.
 \label{cal:bulk-bound}
\end{aligned}$$ In particular the nonnegative potential $$Q_t(z):=\int_{O_t}G_t(z,w)|M_t(w)|^2\,\mathrm dA(w)
 \quad\text{satisfies}\quad 0\leq Q_t(z)\leq\frac1{4m}.
 \label{cal:bounded-potential}$$

On every such stopped interval $[0,T]$, $$\mathbb E\int_0^T\int_{O_t}G_t(z,w)
                         \,\mathrm d[M(w),\overline{M(w)}]_t\,\mathrm dA(w)<\infty.
 \label{cal:weighted-bracket}$$ The potential $Q_t(z)$ has a continuous semimartingale version, and $$\begin{aligned}
 \mathrm dQ_t(z)={}&-\frac2\pi P_t(z)
       \left(\int_{O_t}P_t(w)|M_t(w)|^2\,\mathrm dA(w)\right)\mathrm dt
 \notag\\
 &+\int_{O_t}G_t(z,w)\,\mathrm d[M(w),\overline{M(w)}]_t\,\mathrm dA(w)
 \notag\\
 &+2\operatorname{Re}\int_{O_t}
                G_t(z,w)\overline{M_t(w)}\,\mathrm dM_t(w)\,\mathrm dA(w).
 \label{cal:potential-differential}
\end{aligned}$$ The last line is defined by the weighted bracket-isometry limit of compactly supported stochastic integrals. The statement holds simultaneously for countably many protected spatial points, and also as a spatial distribution identity on protected open sets.
The continuous process $W$ is a semimartingale in the joint filtration.

Locally in time there is a continuous increasing process $L$ such that $\mathrm dt$, $|\mathrm dV|$, $\mathrm d[W^{\mathrm M}]$, and all the spatial bracket measures used below are absolutely continuous with respect to $\mathrm dL$. Outside one null set for $\mathrm dL\,\mathrm d\mathbb P$, write $$\tau=\frac{\mathrm dt}{\mathrm dL},\qquad \nu=\frac{\mathrm dV}{\mathrm dL},\qquad U=\dot W^{\mathrm M},\qquad A_{\mathrm{phys}}(w)=\dot M(w). \label{cal:clock-notation}$$ The dots denote covariance vectors with respect to $\mathrm dL$, not time derivatives. These vectors lie in a real Hilbert space, complexified for $A_{\mathrm{phys}}$. Their scalar products are the corresponding bracket densities. The product is extended bilinearly, so $A\cdot\overline A=|A|^2$ and $U\cdot U=|U|^2$. The field $A_{\mathrm{phys}}$ is spatially smooth on every compact subset of the live domain. Spatial evaluations, derivatives, compact tests, and the Green stochastic integrals in [cal:potential-differential] have their covariance vectors on this same full set. In particular, for protected $z$, $$\int_{O_t}G_t(z,w)|A_{\mathrm{phys}}(w)|^2\,\mathrm dA(w)<\infty \quad\text{for }\mathrm dL\text{-almost every live time.} \label{cal:clock-green-integrability}$$

In the current conformal setting, assume [cal:mu-L2], [cal:weighted-A], and the bulk bound $|F(v)|^2\leq K/\operatorname{Im}v$ from [cal:poisson-control]. Then [cal:identity-zero]–[cal:identity-drift] imply $$\begin{aligned} F(z)^2&=\frac1{\pi z}+o(s^{-1}) \qquad\text{uniformly on }B_s, \label{cal:tip-leading}\\ 2F(z)A(z)&=\frac U{\pi z^2}+o(s^{-3/2}) \qquad\text{in }L^2_{\rm av}(B_s), \label{cal:tip-mixed-weak}\\ \int_{\mathbb H}DG(z,v)\mu(v)|A(v)|^2\,\mathrm dA(v) &=o(s^{-2}) \qquad\text{in }L^1_{\rm av}(B_s). \label{cal:tip-bracket} \end{aligned}$$ If in addition $J=\int_{\mathbb H}\mu(v)|v|^{-2}\,\mathrm dA(v)<\infty$, then $$\begin{aligned} F(z)^2&=\frac1{\pi z}+C+o(1) \qquad\text{uniformly on }B_s, \label{cal:tip-constant}\\ 2F(z)A(z)&=\frac U{\pi z^2}+o(s^{-1}) \qquad\text{in }L^2_{\rm av}(B_s). \label{cal:tip-mixed-strong} \end{aligned}$$ No finiteness of $J$ is required for [cal:tip-leading]–[cal:tip-bracket].

There is a fixed nonanticipating progressively measurable extension of $C_t$ to continuous driving paths, agreeing with Equation [mod:C] whenever its integral is finite. The same extension can be used for every candidate law in Definition 3.
Definition 3 determines exactly one law. Every admissible approximation whose physical domains have a common diameter bound converges to this law in the disc curve topology.

For every connected interior arc $E_n\subset\Omega_n\setminus
B(0,S-1)$, its disc image has diameter tending to zero, uniformly over the choice of arc. The same is true for the noncentral shadow of a crosscut contained there.*

*More precisely, fix a point $\xi\in\partial\mathbb D$, a positive parameter tolerance $a$, and a positive physical tolerance $\rho$. For all sufficiently large $n$, one can choose $s_n$ in a fixed interval $[s_-,s_+]\subset(0,a)$ such that the entire preimage of $\partial B(\xi,s_n)\cap\mathbb D$ is contained in $B(0,S-2)$ and has length at most $\rho$. The endpoints and shadows are understood in the prime-end compactification. The conclusion holds simultaneously for finitely many specified $\xi$’s, with disjoint parameter caps when those points are distinct.

Let $V_n\subset\mathbb D$ be the simply connected component containing $0$ after removing finitely many closed, piecewise analytic obstructions and filling the other components. Assume that the obstructions lie within distance $\varepsilon_n\to0$ of $\partial\mathbb D$, and that every point on an obstruction can be joined to $\mathbb C\setminus\mathbb D$ within the removed set by a connected set of diameter at most $\varepsilon_n$. Then the normalized maps $F_n:\mathbb D\to V_n$ satisfy $$\sup_{\overline\mathbb D}|F_n(z)-z|\longrightarrow0.
 \label{loc:maps-identity}$$ For every prime-end occurrence $w=F_n(\zeta)$, this also gives $|F_n^{-1}(w)-w|\to0$, uniformly. The same conclusion holds for any number of such obstructions; no bound on their number or total length is required.

Let $U_{n,j}$ be the component of $\Omega_n\cap B(0,s_j)$ containing $0$. Its visible exit arcs on $\partial B(0,s_j)$ are crosscuts of the initial domain, with pairwise disjoint noncentral shadows. Every point of $\Omega_n$ outside that circle lies behind one mandatory visible gate: every path from $0$ to that point crosses it. A gate at a later level has one specified ancestor gate at every earlier level.*

*Call a gate at level $j$ large when its length is at least $2^{-j}$. There are at most $K_S2^j$ large gates at that level. A chain of small ancestors at levels $j$ gives disjoint annuli centered on those ancestors, with inner radii $K2^{-j}$ and outer radii $c_0(j+2)^{-2}$, for all sufficiently large $j$. Every path from a circle-$S$ portal to a point of radius $S+2$, continued to $0$ within $B(0,S)$, crosses these annuli.

For every sufficiently small parameter tolerance $a>0$, the two ends can be explored, each stopped before its first unpeeled cell on a protected fence, with the following properties:*

1.  *Each explored head has disc diameter at most $Ka+o(1)$. The two heads lie in disjoint endpoint neighborhoods.*

2.  *The center has unqueried connected access chains to the two resulting front corners. These chains lie in $B(0,S-1)$ and on the inner side of every proposed small $H$-cap and of the circle at $S$.*

3.  *Conditional on these local revelations, the connecting problem is an ordinary Dobrushin problem. In the initial disc its changes are attached obstructions of diameter at most $Ka+o(1)$, with fillings behind them.*

*The preimages of the $H$-cap cuts can subsequently be chosen to have any prescribed small physical diameter $\rho>0$, while retaining these properties and containing the large gates at levels $j\le J$.

Let a distal cap have boundary color $c$, with its portal strictly inside the physical cutoff $S+3$. There is a finite edge exploration on its distal side with the following alternatives.*

1.  *On success, all retained parts of the cap have radius less than $S+3+K\delta_n$. The new retained boundary is made of $c$-open diagonals attached to the original $c$-bank. Every queried edge lies outside or on that boundary, so the retained connecting problem has its ordinary Dobrushin conditional law.*

2.  *Failure implies an actual opposite-color path from radius at least $S+3-K\delta_n$ to cells incident to the portal, with an endpoint error of at most $K\delta_n$.*

*The same statements hold for all caps explored in a fixed order, stopping the entire surgery at its first failure. Conditioning on the complete successful revelation record imposes no further event on the unqueried central edges.

From every admissible approximation sequence one can extract a further subsequence and perform finite edge revelations with success probability tending to one, so that on success:*

1.  *the unqueried connecting domain $\widehat\Omega_n$ is a Dobrushin polygon on the original mesh with the same thermal parameters and diameter at most $2S+20$;*

2.  *conditional on the complete revelation record, its interface has the ordinary Dobrushin FK law;*

3.  *every deterministic sequence of possible successful outputs $(\widehat\Omega_n,\widehat a_n,\widehat b_n)$ converges in the marked Carathéodory sense to $(\Omega,a,b)$;*

4.  *the normalized coordinates on the retained domain are uniformly $o(1)$ from its original normalized coordinates, including prime-end occurrences, and the removed endpoint heads have vanishing disc diameter.*

*All error bounds are uniform over successful outcomes.
For $m>0$, every approximation sequence in Theorem 1 converges to the law of Definition 3, in the specified normalized-disc curve topology.

The choice of $\phi$ is immaterial. Replacing it by $\lambda\phi$, $\lambda>0$, replaces $t,W_t,v$ by $\lambda^2t,\lambda W_t,\lambda v$. Directly from Equation [mod:C], the new coefficient at time $\lambda^2t$ is $C_t/\lambda$. Brownian scaling therefore preserves Equation [mod:SDE] and its finite-energy condition. The initial disc normalization similarly provides coordinates for the curve topology, rather than extra data for the law.

The noncircular-bank hypothesis is a statement about the accessible side of the bank. A vertex identified with another occurrence on the far side of a slit does not supply an accessible wire of color $c$. One first works in incident sectors and then makes the monotone identification in the proof. Likewise an incident determined diagonal of color $c$ would expose its own color on an accessible bank; it cannot be silently placed on a bank declared to have the other color. Buffering by more than the diameter of the local cell templates removes the only ambiguity at the circular ends.

The scalar field $h_t$ and its square derivative are functions of the current marked domain. Their interior data are kernel-continuous, and integrals of nonnegative functions of them are measurable by compact exhaustion. A signed lift need not be selected as a continuous deterministic function of every possible curve; the joint-limit construction in Proposition 14 is enough for stochastic calculus. The geometric estimates in Corollary 13 are needed only in the natural driver filtration. Their unconditional integrability consequences remain valid on adjoining the signed field, without an assertion that arbitrary filtration enlargements preserve conditional crossing estimates.

The estimate holds on the entire capacity half-line. Neither an exponential-martingale estimate nor any absolute continuity with a Brownian-driven law was used in obtaining it. Its geometric inputs remain uniform after live restarts, and every conformal-radius infimum was taken before swallowing. These two features are what make the estimate available for the subsequent potential calculus.

The uniqueness argument localizes energy on finite capacity horizons. It needs neither a global Novikov condition nor a comparison of complete infinite-horizon curve laws. In particular, no assertion of mutual absolute continuity at infinite capacity is used in Theorem 1.

Both lemmas apply to the cell collars used below. In the initial disc, each retained cell sector has vanishing diameter by Lemma 10. A boundary cell is attached to the old boundary through its own sector. Filling behind a boundary pinch is covered by the first paragraph of Lemma 35. The finite-arc boundary condition in that lemma is imposed only on the approximating polygons and their conformal images, not on the limiting domain $\Omega$.
